derivation.behavior: FTP/FTPS downloads use canonical attempt/checkpoint/verification lifecycle.
derivation.canonical_behavior: Go FTP adapter reuses limiter, retry taxonomy, staging, verification and publication infrastructure.

invariants: FTP and FTPS consume canonical NetworkIntent rather than a protocol-specific request model.
FTP passwords are resolved from opaque credential references at execution time; anonymous login remains explicit and deterministic.
Resume uses REST only for bodyless GET semantics and writes response bytes through canonical durable checkpoint commits.
Connection and byte accounting use the shared transfer resource limiter contract.
Disconnects and unsupported server features are represented through typed engine failures rather than string matching.
Transport completion remains nonterminal until canonical checksum verification and publication preparation succeed.
